citations.quote:
Fix $c>0$ and take $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,\mathbf x)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and future causal cone $\{V\in\mathbb R^4:V^0\geq0,\ \eta_{ab}V^aV^b\leq0\}$. For $V^0>0$, membership in this cone is exactly the coordinate-speed condition $|d\mathbf x/dt|\leq c$; its boundary speed is the reference speed $c$. The constant rest observer is $\bar u=(1,0,0,0)$.

Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be open, let $e\in C^2(X;\mathbb R)$, and fix $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})\in X$. Define $n_0:=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0:=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $p_0:=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $T_0:=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $h_0:=\epsilon_0+p_0$. Assume $n_0,T_0,h_0,e_{vv}>0$, with $e_{vv}$ evaluated at fixed $\sigma_p$. A first variation is defined by a family of state maps $(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda}):M\to X$ and fields $u_\lambda:M\to\mathbb R^4$, jointly smooth in dimensionless $\lambda$ near $0$ and in $x$, with the displayed reference state and $\bar u$ as their constant $\lambda=0$ values and with $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$, $u_\lambda^0>0$. For any such field $f_\lambda$, write $\delta f:=\left.\partial_\lambda f_\lambda\right|_{\lambda=0}$; put $r:=\delta\epsilon$, $w:=(\delta u^1,\delta u^2,\delta u^3)$, and impose the adiabatic first-variation condition $\delta\sigma_p=0$. The linearized equations mean the first variations at $\lambda=0$ of the no-force balances $\partial_aT_\lambda^{ab}=0$ and $\partial_aJ_\lambda^a=0$, with $n_\lambda=1/v_\lambda$, $\epsilon_\lambda=n_\lambda e(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $p_\lambda=-e_v(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $\Delta_\lambda^{ab}=\eta^{ab}+u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b$, $T_\lambda^{ab}=\epsilon_\lambda u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b+p_\lambda\Delta_\lambda^{ab}$, and $J_\lambda^a=n_\lambda u_\lambda^a$; no member with $\lambda\ne0$ is required to solve the nonlinear balances. Differentiating $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$ gives $\delta u^0=0$.

The local Gibbs identity of [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]] gives

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})}{n_0h_0},$$

and assume additionally $a_s\le1$. In the adopted units, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $r$ and $h_0$ have units Pa, and $w$ and $a_s$ are dimensionless. Since $x^0=ct$ and $\bar u=\partial_{x^0}$, the first variations of the no-force perfect-fluid projection equations of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] are

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c a_s}{h_0}\nabla r=0.$$

For initial data $U_0=(r_0,w_0)$ whose real components belong componentwise to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$ as defined by [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], or for smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$ with $L>0$, these equations have the unique global smooth solution supplied by [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]]. The positive quadratic energy density $\mathcal E=\tfrac12[(a_s/h_0)r^2+h_0|w|^2]$ has flux $c a_s r w$, and the solution is contractive in the corresponding weighted $L^2$ and Sobolev norms. Its characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm c\sqrt{a_s}$; for positive $a_s$, this propagation cone lies inside the Minkowski reference cone exactly when $a_s\le1$. These are statements about this frozen linear system only; they do not assert a nonlinear or curved-spacetime evolution theorem.

For the formal coefficient comparison in [A3], if the same linear equations are assigned $a_s>1$, their plane-wave speed is $c\sqrt{a_s}>c$. If they are assigned $a_s<0$, smooth periodic modes grow as $e^{c\sqrt{-a_s}|k|t}$ at arbitrarily large wave numbers. The case $a_s=0$ is degenerate: the displayed positive energy matrix is no longer positive definite, so the stability proof above does not apply.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Let $c>0$ be a fixed speed parameter, use Minkowski coordinates $x^0=ct$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and consider a smooth perfect-fluid state at a uniform rest point. The local state has energy per marker $e\in C^2(X)$ on an open domain $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, with specific volume $v=1/n$ and specific entropy $\sigma_p$; $e_{vv}$ denotes the second derivative at fixed $\sigma_p$. At the rest point assume $n_0>0$, $T_0>0$, $h_0=\epsilon_0+p_0>0$, and $e_{vv}>0$. Let

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n_0h_0},$$

as in [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]], and assume additionally $a_s\le1$. For adiabatic perturbations $\delta\sigma_p=0$, write $r=\delta\epsilon$ and $w=\delta u_{\rm spatial}\in\mathbb R^3$. The linearized equations obtained from the no-force perfect stress and particle balances of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] are

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c a_s}{h_0}\nabla r=0.$$

For Schwartz data on $\mathbb R^3$ or smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$, these equations have the unique global smooth solution supplied by [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]]. The positive quadratic energy density $\mathcal E=\tfrac12[(a_s/h_0)r^2+h_0|w|^2]$ has flux $c a_s r w$, and the solution is contractive in the corresponding weighted $L^2$ and Sobolev norms. Its characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm c\sqrt{a_s}$; for positive $a_s$, this cone lies inside the reference cone of speed $c$ exactly when $a_s\le1$. These are statements about this frozen linear system only; they do not assert a nonlinear or curved-spacetime evolution theorem.

For the formal coefficient comparison in [A3], if the same linear equations are assigned $a_s>1$, their plane-wave speed is $c\sqrt{a_s}>c$. If they are assigned $a_s<0$, smooth periodic modes grow as $e^{c\sqrt{-a_s}|k|t}$ at arbitrarily large wave numbers. The case $a_s=0$ is degenerate: the displayed positive energy matrix is no longer positive definite, so the stability proof above does not apply.

for the bulk-only branch.

Use $\mathcal M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,\mathbf x)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, future direction $\partial_{x^0}$, and reference causal cone $\{V:V^0\geq0,\ \eta_{ab}V^aV^b\leq0\}$, whose boundary speed in $(t,\mathbf x)$ coordinates is $c$. Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be open, $e\in C^2(X;\mathbb R)$, and $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})\in X$. Define $n_0:=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0:=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $p_0:=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $T_0:=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $h_0:=\epsilon_0+p_0$. The background fields are this constant state, $u_0=\partial_{x^0}=(1,0,0,0)$, and $\Pi_0=0$. Assume $n_0,T_0,h_0,e_{vv},c>0$, with $e_{vv}$ evaluated at fixed $\sigma_p$.

A first variation is defined by a family $(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda},u_\lambda,\Pi_\lambda)$ jointly smooth in dimensionless $\lambda$ near $0$ and in $x$, through the displayed background, with $u_\lambda$ future unit, meaning $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$ and $u_\lambda^0>0$. For any such field $f_\lambda$, set $\delta f:=\left.\partial_\lambda f_\lambda\right|_{\lambda=0}$. At each $\lambda$, set $n_\lambda=1/v_\lambda$, $\epsilon_\lambda=n_\lambda e(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $p_\lambda=-e_v(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $T_\lambda=e_{\sigma_p}(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $\Delta_\lambda^{ab}=\eta^{ab}+u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b$, $D_\lambda=u_\lambda^a\partial_a$, and $\theta_\lambda=\partial_a u_\lambda^a$. The bulk stress and current are $T_\lambda^{ab}=\epsilon_\lambda u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b+(p_\lambda+\Pi_\lambda)\Delta_\lambda^{ab}$ and $J_\lambda^a=n_\lambda u_\lambda^a$, and the corrected law of [[lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy]] is $\beta D_\lambda\Pi_\lambda+\Pi_\lambda/(\zeta c)=-\theta_\lambda-(T_\lambda\Pi_\lambda/2)\partial_a(\beta u_\lambda^a/T_\lambda)$, where $\beta=\tau/\zeta$. The linearized equations mean the first variations at $\lambda=0$ of $\partial_aT_\lambda^{ab}=0$, $\partial_aJ_\lambda^a=0$, and this corrected law, set equal to zero; no member with $\lambda\ne0$ is required to solve the nonlinear system. Impose $\delta\sigma_p=0$, put $r:=\delta\epsilon$, $w:=(\delta u^1,\delta u^2,\delta u^3)$, and denote $\delta\Pi$ by $\Pi$ in the linearized system below. Take constant coefficients $\zeta,\tau>0$.

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n_0h_0}>0$$

as supplied by [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]]. The resulting linearized system is

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c}{h_0}\nabla(a_s r+\Pi)=0,\qquad \tau\Pi_t+\Pi=-\zeta c\operatorname{div}w.$$

Its positive quadratic energy density

$$\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}=\frac12\left[\frac{a_s}{h_0}r^2+h_0|w|^2+\frac{\tau}{\zeta}\Pi^2\right]$$

satisfies $\partial_t\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}+\operatorname{div}[c(a_s r+\Pi)w]=-\Pi^2/\zeta$. The normal characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm v_{\rm bulk}$, where

$$v_{\rm bulk}=c\sqrt{a_s+\frac{\zeta}{\tau h_0}}.$$

By [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]], initial data $U_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^5)$ with the componentwise real convention of [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], or smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$ with $L>0$, have unique global smooth solutions, contractive in the corresponding energy and Sobolev norms, with finite propagation at $v_{\rm bulk}$. The branch is inside the Minkowski reference cone exactly when $a_s+\zeta/(\tau h_0)\le1$. Constant density and transverse velocity modes can persist, so contraction does not mean every mode decays. No nonlinear or variable-coefficient existence theorem is claimed.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
